images.title: Six 8s grouped two ways
images.purpose: Shows the same six factors of 8 grouped as three pairs, (8²)³, and as two triples, (8³)².
images.composition: Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text. The power 8⁶ at the top centre and two identical rows of six tiles below it, each grouped differently.
images.exact_structure: Top centre: the label '8⁶' in large type. Row 1: exactly 6 equal square tiles each showing '8', grouped by 3 teal (#0072B2) rounded outlines, each around 2 neighbouring tiles; the label '(8²)³' to the right of the row. Row 2, directly below: exactly 6 equal square tiles each showing '8', grouped by 2 amber (#E69F00) rounded outlines, each around 3 neighbouring tiles; the label '(8³)²' to the right of the row. Exactly 12 tiles, 5 outlines.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: Split the exponent into two factors to write a power as a power of a power.
images.description: Shows the same six factors of 8 grouped as three pairs, (8²)³, and as two triples, (8³)².
images.context: 6 = 2 × 3 = 3 × 2, so 8 to the power 6 is (8²)³ and (8³)². Since 8 = 2³, it is also 2 to the power 18.
images.teaching_notes: Label '8' appears on all 12 tiles. Try 5 to the power 8 as (5²)⁴ and (5⁴)².

image_decisions.why: Grouping the same factors in two ways shows how one power becomes a power of a power in two forms.
